title: Meta was prepared to write an up to $200 billion AI check before knowing whether its model would work
content:
Mark Zuckerberg was ready to bet as much as $200 billion on AI, and Meta’s finance chief wanted the person building it to understand what failure would mean.
On the Cheeky Pint podcast released on Monday, Meta CEO and Alexandr Wang, Meta's chief AI officer, recounted conversations from late last year about enormous investments before Meta’s new models had proven themselves.
“At the end of last year, we're like, all right, we are quite excited about the progress. We haven't seen the models yet,” Zuckerberg told show host John Collison.
“I'm going to, like, you know, we're going to write this check for, like, I don't know, like $100 billion, $200 billion. I'm like, 'Alex, are you sure this is going to work?'” Zuckerberg said of Wang.
Zuckerberg did not specify the timeframe or exact scope of that contemplated commitment.
Wang said he had encouraging research updates at that point, but success was far from certain. At an executive gathering in Hawaii, Wang said that CFO Susan Li repeatedly pulled him aside.
“Susan pulled me aside many times and was like, 'You know, I just want to tell you, if this doesn't work, like, you know, this is going to be really, really bad. It's going to be very, very bad in financial terms.'” Wang said of Li.
Meta's capex over the past few quarters has been substantial, raising eyebrows among investors. Meta’s latest guidance puts 2026 capital expenditures, including finance lease principal payments, at $130 billion to $145 billion. In forecasts previously seen by Business Insider, Cantor Fitzgerald analysts expect the spending to reach $200 billion in 2027.
Investors have shown limits. Meta shares fell more than 6% in after-hours trading following April’s earnings report, despite strong results, after the company raised its annual spending forecast to $125 billion to $145 billion.
Inside Meta, the leadership is well aware of the stakes. In Wang's words, "this is a fuck ton of risk.”
"So I think that in order for it not to work out, it's not just that we have to fail, AI overall has to fail," Zuckerberg said. "And then even if that happens, we still have all these other uses to productively use compute."

report.summary: 扎克伯格曾准备在模型未验证前向AI投入至多2000亿美元。
report.background: 2025年底，Meta在自研大模型尚未证明效果时就计划进行史上最大规模AI资本押注。CEO扎克伯格向首席AI官Alexandr Wang询问规模1000亿至2000亿美元投入的可行性，CFO Susan Li则多次警告失败将带来严重财务后果。此前Meta已大幅上调资本支出预期，2026年指引为1300亿至1450亿美元，分析师预计2027年将达2000亿美元。投资者对此已有反应，Meta股价曾在财报后下跌超6%。这一事件折射出科技巨头在AI竞赛中'先下注、后验证'的普遍博弈心态。
key_points: 扎克伯格在自研模型尚未问世时，就准备签下1000亿至2000亿美元的AI投资支票，属于典型的高风险豪赌。
Meta CFO Susan Li多次私下警告首席AI官：如果项目失败，财务后果将'非常非常糟糕'，说明内部对风险有清醒认识。
Meta资本支出持续膨胀，2026年预计达1300亿至1450亿美元，分析师预计2027年进一步升至2000亿美元。
投资者已表现出耐心上限，Meta上调支出预期后股价盘后下跌超6%，市场对无底洞式投入保持警惕。
扎克伯格认为除非整个AI行业都失败，否则这笔投入不会打水漂，即使模型失败，算力仍可用于其他产品。
该项目由Meta首席AI官Alexandr Wang主导，当时只有'令人鼓舞'的研究进展，成功远未确定。
report.impact: 对AI行业而言，这标志着头部公司进入'不计成本抢位'阶段，可能进一步推高算力、人才和能源价格，并加剧中小玩家的竞争压力。对开发者来说，巨头持续烧钱意味着工具链、开源模型和API生态会加速迭代，但就业与创业方向将更依赖巨头生态。对普通用户，短期会享受更便宜甚至免费的AI功能，但长期需关注市场集中度和服务涨价风险。
report.tools: 想跟进可关注Meta的Llama系列开源模型、PyTorch生态及Meta AI官方博客；关注AI算力成本可参考SemiAnalysis、Epoch AI等分析平台；投资人可跟踪Meta财报电话会中的capex指引和Cantor Fitzgerald等机构研报。
